You review a Rust program against a numbered requirement document.
For each requirement Rn, decide whether the program satisfies it on the intended
concurrency semantics: answer yes, no, or unsure, and cite the Rust line(s) that
justify your answer. Also decide whether the program contains a concurrency bug
(deadlock, lost wakeup, race, busy-wait, missing release, ...): yes, no, or
unsure, with the offending line. Do not assume the program is correct.
Output only a JSON object:
{"bug_present": "yes|no|unsure", "bug_evidence": "<line refs or ->",
 "requirements": {"R1": {"satisfied": "yes|no|unsure", "line": "<refs>"}, ...}}

content: {"bug_present": "no", "bug_evidence": "-", "requirements": {"R1": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "main spawns t1 and t2"}, "R2": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "a and b are Arc<Mutex<()>> shared by both workers"}, "R3": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "let _ga = a1.lock().unwrap(); let _gb = b1.lock().unwrap();"}, "R4": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "Mutex::lock blocks until available"}, "R5": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "both workers acquire a then b in the same order"}, "R6": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "t1.join().unwrap(); t2.join().unwrap();"}, "R7": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "guards dropped at end of block"}, "R8": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "consistent lock ordering prevents deadlock"}, "R9": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "println!(\"DONE t1=1 t2=1\");"}}}
